items.prompt: A pattern is made with counters. Figure 1 has 3 counters and each new figure has 3 more counters than the one before. Describe the first four figures and say how many counters each has.
items.answer: 3, 6, 9 and 12 counters - each figure has 3 more counters than the figure before it.

items.prompt: A pupil predicts that figure 5 of a stick pattern uses 13 sticks. Figure 1 uses 5 sticks and each figure adds 2 sticks. Draw or describe figure 5 and say whether the prediction is right.
items.answer: Figure 5 uses 5 + 4 x 2 = 13 sticks, so the prediction is right.

items.prompt: A pattern of dots grows as 1, 4, 9, 16 ... Describe the next figure in the pattern and say how many dots it has.
items.answer: A square with 5 dots on each side; 25 dots.

items.prompt: A coin is tossed 10 times. It lands on heads 7 times and tails 3 times. Record the results in a table and explain why this does not mean the coin is unfair.
items.answer: Table: heads 7, tails 3. In only 10 tosses a fair coin can still give an uneven result; the more times you toss it, the closer the results get to half and half.

items.prompt: A die is rolled 20 times and the number 6 comes up 6 times. Explain why the results are not exactly the theoretical probability.
items.answer: The theoretical probability of a 6 is 1/6, which is about 3 or 4 times in 20 rolls; in a small experiment the results vary about that value.
